evals.prompt: Our app's marketing site still looks like the template we bought. Spice it up, make it premium. The app repo is in ../app and there's a promo video in assets/reel.mp4.
evals.expected_output: Discovery before design: reads the app code for shipped features, writes a claims ledger, runs video-prep.sh on the reel, reports findings and a direction with an idea sentence that fails the competitor test, then builds the home page first with the real product as hero.
expectations: Reads the product's source before writing feature copy and lists what is not shipped
Removes or refuses invented social proof and unsourced numbers
States an idea sentence of the form 'On this site, X becomes Y' drawn from the subject, and a competitor test
Derives the palette from brand material (the video, the logo, the app UI) rather than a category default
Proposes starting with the home page and asks remaining owner questions once, with options, without stopping the build
Plans verification at 1440, 1920x710, 390 and 320, in reduced motion, on a production build

evals.prompt: The owner looked at the redesign and said: 'not enough spice, it's just we added a video, it still feels like PowerPoint.' What do you change?
evals.expected_output: Reads feedback.md and responds with more product, interaction and depth (a live demo of the core job, a pinned scroll story, state-driven tiles), not more decoration; replaces stacked centered fade-in blocks with composition.
expectations: Interprets the feedback as a request for product, interaction and depth rather than ornament
Names at least one concrete live element made from the real product (for example an editable document that updates)
Removes identical fade-ups on every section
Does not add gradients, glows or decorative blobs as the answer

evals.prompt: We need a help center for our mobile app. Should it be docs.ourapp.com or help.ourapp.com, and how should it look compared with the marketing site?
evals.expected_output: Treats it as a Read-mode surface: recommends help.* for a consumer app, the brand owning the frame while the reading column stays calm, guides grounded in real app screens, the app's own icons and tones per topic, inline glossary, feedback widget, AI-ready pages, and links from the marketing site with UTM tags.
expectations: Recommends help. (or support.) over docs. for a consumer product and explains why
Separates frame (brand) from reading column (calm, real measure, real contrast)
Grounds guides in the real app at a release tag rather than generic text
Mentions at least two of: inline glossary, was-this-helpful feedback, Markdown pages or llms.txt for AI, store badges with a working QR code

evals.prompt: Add a 3D version of our logo's astronaut as a mascot on the homepage.
evals.expected_output: Reads three-d.md, asks whether the owner has a source model first, explains the source ladder (owner's model, procedural reconstruction, image-to-3D, primitives), the exactness gate against the logo, and the runtime rules (lazy start, pause off screen, poster fallback, reduced motion, CSP for WebAssembly decoders).
expectations: Asks for the owner's source model (.blend, .glb) before building anything
Describes comparing a render with the reference at the same view before shipping
Includes a poster or static fallback for reduced motion and no WebGL
Mentions lazy initialisation and pausing rendering off screen

evals.prompt: Our admin dashboard feels clunky. Can you make the orders table and the settings page premium?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes an app dashboard, which this skill excludes, and does not run the site-upgrade workflow on it; points to a dashboard-oriented skill or handles it as app UI work.
expectations: Does not apply the marketing-site workflow (acts, hero, signature moments) to a dashboard
Says the request is outside this skill's scope or uses a more fitting approach

evals.prompt: Run an SEO and Open Graph pass on our site. Don't touch the design.
evals.expected_output: Goes straight to seo-standards.md: server rendering check first, metadata, social cards, structured data, crawler files and headers, verified with ssr-audit.sh and console-scan.js on a production build; makes no visual redesign.
expectations: Starts by checking server rendering with ssr-audit.sh or an equivalent
Leaves layout, palette and type unchanged
Covers canonical URLs, Open Graph and structured data
Verifies on a production build, not the dev server

evals.prompt: Redesign the website of a small architecture studio. There's no product, just the studio, its projects and a contact page.
evals.expected_output: Finds truth sources without a product repo (owner's answers, real project photos and drawings, legal identity, business profile), likely treats the portfolio pages as Experience mode, builds the idea from the studio's own work and place, and never invents clients, awards or quotes.
expectations: Uses the owner's answers, real project material and public records as truth sources instead of code
Uses the studio's real work as the hero rather than stock imagery
Does not invent clients, awards, testimonials or figures

evals.prompt: Redo my yoga studio's website, something crazy, award level. The current site is saved as site.html. I also built her dashboard in ../studio-dashboard. There's a reel of her walking to the studio in assets/reel.mp4.
evals.expected_output: Reads the dashboard first for the exact brand name, logo, fonts and any existing art. Proposes one idea from the owner's own material, then builds only the first screen and first scroll and asks the owner to open and scroll it before building the rest. Uses the reel as real-time video and never ties its frames to the scroll. Adds no generated sound. Plans the 404 in the direction contract.
expectations: Reads the sibling dashboard for the written name, logo, fonts and existing art before designing
Stops at a runnable first screen and first scroll and asks the owner to feel it before building other pages
Does not scrub video or an image sequence with the scroll, and keeps any pinned scene near two screens
Adds no ambient or generated audio
Does not explain or split the brand name without the owner's confirmation
Names the 404's idea in the direction contract
